handoff: Two blocking: lost path skips the post-claim record-ref re-read (race hides a pushed record, checkout.ts:378); no test proves the restart step comes from the last boundary (AC1/AC3 both expect the start step). Fetch failure vs absent ref is handled correctly. 8 minor/nit.

findings.title: Restart step from the last boundary is untraced
findings.detail:
AC1: 'starts a new round ... at the last Norn-Step trailer's step'. AC1's test (A at implement after a review rework) and AC3's test both expect `implement`, which is rv's `start`. If restartStepOf (packages/core/src/apply.ts:66) always returned wf.start, or lastBoundary (checkout.ts:257) were dropped, all tests pass. No unit test of restartStepOf exists (Norn-Next, older-boundary fallback to `ended`, step not in workflow -> start).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add a case where A dies at review (last boundary implement.done, Norn-Next review) and B's checkout restarts review; add core unit tests of restartStepOf for next / ended-only / missing step -> start.

findings.title: No post-claim re-check of the record ref on the lost path (race hides a real record)
findings.detail:
The review#2 F5 guard `if (remote && staged && prepared)` re-reads remoteRecordSha after the CAS only when a record was staged. When `lost`, prepared is null, so nothing checks that the ref is still absent after the claim. A holder that runs `story handoff` (pushes refs/norn/runs/<story>, then deletes its claim) or still runs under remote policy between prepareRecord's ls-remote and a --force/expired CAS lets B start a new round that hides the real record and its history: exactly the misfire the step was asked to rule out.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: When `lost`, after the claim re-read remoteRecordSha; if it is not null (or the read fails), give the claim back (when not mine) and refuse `record_moved` as the staged path does. Test it with a ref pushed between the fetch and the claim (as the F5 test does).

findings.title: A non-holder's stale local run state is replaced whole on the lost path
findings.detail:
keepLocal = mine && exists. When the claim is not this checkout's but storyRunStateDir exists (an earlier hold here), stageEmptyRecord + place (line 396) replace it; the only surviving copy of the history may go. The ref path replaces it the same way and setting it aside is gh-195/14 (slice Scope: 'Out: setting the old holder's copy aside (gh-195/14)'), so not blocking here; make sure 14 covers the lost path too.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Route to gh-195/14 explicitly (lost path included).

findings.title: Unparsable frontmatter on the branch read as 'not started'
findings.detail:
`if (!fm?.ok || status !== 'active') return null` treats a corrupt spec frontmatter like an unstarted story: the take goes through with no record and no refusal (S2: a failing file is refused, never guessed around).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Refuse (e.g. corrupt/spec_invalid) when the file exists and fails to parse; keep null only for a valid non-active frontmatter.

findings.title: lastBoundary swallows a git log failure
findings.detail:
A failing git log returns null, so restartStepOf silently falls back to wf.start and a lost-record take restarts at the first step with no notice.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Let the error surface on the lost path (refuse before the claim) or at least say so in the restarted line.

findings.title: workflow_invalid refusal and non-active skip untested
findings.detail:
The refusals before the claim ('nothing was taken') for a missing or invalid workflow on the branch, and the skip for a non-active frontmatter, have no test.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Add an integration case: invalid/missing workflow on the branch -> exit refused, code workflow_invalid, no claim on the remote, no run state.

findings.title: Crash between claim and place leaks a staging folder
findings.detail:
A crash after the claim and before fresh.place() leaves `.<dir>.unpack-<pid>`; recoverPlace cleans only the aside folder and mkdirSync(recursive) would reuse leftovers. A rerun does recover (claim mine, no state, no ref -> new round again), at the cost of a leaked folder and a second take trace event.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Sweep stale `.unpack-*` folders in recoverPlace, or create the staging dir exclusively.

findings.title: Tautological assertion on the record_only push
findings.detail:
`expect([pushed, ...]).toContain(pushed)` is always true, so the record push on handoff of a record_only story is not asserted (only the claim release is).
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Assert `after === pushed` or that `after^` equals pushed, whichever is meant.

findings.title: record_only story: list shows branch 'gh-21-', status shows the old run running
findings.detail:
Not against B25/B26 (spec out of scope: 'Intake of a story without a branch (#126) — only where its record lives is covered'), but both contradict the recordOnly doc 'Nothing runs in it until it has a branch'; the test at takeover-record.test.ts:339 pins 'review #2 (auto)'.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: File as a separate issue (friction/bug); do not pin the running display as intended.

findings.title: Duplicated head rev-parse
findings.detail:
`headRef`/`tip` re-derive and re-rev-parse what `head` (line 351) already resolved; `branch && headRef` is checked twice; the transcript shows the extra rev-parse.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Compute headRef once and reuse head.

findings.title: --force on one's own wiped claim is per spec
findings.detail:
B26: '`story checkout --force` on that same machine'; T5b agrees. No change needed.
Axis: spec
